newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung confident China to approve top officials.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung confident China to approve top officials.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Tuesday he was confident Beijing would approve his choice of top officials for his post-handover administration when he visits the Chinese capital later this week.
"I think the central authorities have already expressed confidence in me and the Hong Kong people. Therefore, I am confident of my nominations," Tung told a news conference.
But the territory's chief executive designate sidestepped questions of what he would do if Beijing rejected his choices.
"I think you are really speculating. Let us wait until the result comes out," he said.
Tung will fly to the Chinese capital on Wednesday to seek approval from Beijing on his choices of top officials to serve after Britain hands Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30.

The former shipping tycoon declined to say whether he would announce his team of officials after coming back to the territory on Thursday, saying Chinese authorities may take more time to examine his nominations.
Tung also declined to respond to questions on whether all principal officials would stay on as reported in local press.

The outgoing British colonial administration has urged Tung to make as few changes as possible in the ranks of top civil servants, who hold positions akin to cabinet ministers in Britain and wield considerable power.

Tung won public acclaim when he invited Hong Kong's popular Chief Secretary Anson Chan, head of the civil service and deputy to British governor Chris Patten, to stay on, guaranteeing continuity in uncertain times.
She accepted, but the fate of her senior policy secretaries has not yet been decided.
Tung named his inner circle of advisers, or Executive Council, last month.
The list included two members who currently serve on the colonial Governor's Executive Council.
